answer: On a coastal station where cattle graze the salt meadow behind the reef, every animal carries a ferrous ear tag whose 840 number is bound to one premises ID in the national animal disease traceability registry. The state brand inspector checks that tag against the brand registration and the sale barn inspection certificate, and a duplicate 840 number quarantines the whole consignment, fines the dealer and calls the surety bond. Each cloned tag costs 4 dollars for the tag, 60 for the brand filing and 15 for inspection, so a thousand fakes burn 79000 dollars before one head is real.
